prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an elevated viewpoint (around 2–3 m above a workshop floor) looking down at a nearby machine and stacked blue trays on the lower left (1–2 m away), a wheeled cart of trays in the middle ground (3–5 m away), and tall block stacks in the background (6–10 m away). Four people are visible below: a closer left worker by the machine (2–3 m away, within arm's reach of the machine and stacked trays), a farther left worker behind the machine (5–6 m away), a central worker standing beside and partly occluded by the wheeled cart (4–5 m away, within arm's reach of the cart), and a right-side worker in a red shirt who walks from roughly 6 m away in frame 1 to 1.5–2 m below the camera wearer in frame 5 while carrying blue containers. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer turns downward and rightward while extending their right arm into the lower-right foreground in frames 4 and 5 (brightest region at 0.3–0.8 m, reaching within arm's reach of the blue container held up by the approaching red-shirted worker). Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the elevated foreground machinery and extended arm from the sloping ground plane and background walls despite dark shadows on the floor. However, the depth map is unreliable in the last frame where the overall scene scale shifts darker, and fine open-grid structures on the wheeled cart and distant dark corridors merge into blurry, flat depth blocks.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates selected people and objects against the black background across the elevated workshop scene, tracking the right-side worker in the red shirt (pink mask in frames 1–4, light-blue in frame 5) as he approaches from about 6 m to 1.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer, alongside the central worker behind the cart (brown mask, ~1 m left of the red-shirted worker in frame 1 and growing to 2–3 m behind him by frame 4). In the first two frames, it also segments the closer left worker at the machine (2–3 m away) and mislabels a machine component or tray stack near the farther left worker (5–6 m away) as a 'suitcase', while in frame 5 it segments the camera wearer's own extended right arm in the bottom-right corner (0.3–0.8 m away) touching the blue container held up by the red-shirted worker. The masks show the red-shirted worker moving from right-of-center in the background to the lower-right foreground while facing and looking upward toward the camera wearer in frames 4 and 5, whereas the other three workers face sideways toward the machinery and cart and become partly cropped at the upper-left edge in frame 5. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to distinguish the overlapping silhouettes of the central cart worker and the red-shirted worker in frames 1 and 2 and to isolate the camera wearer's reaching arm in frame 5. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable for scene completeness: it completely misses the wheeled cart, background block walls, and most machinery, drops the closer left worker after frame 2, fragments the left worker and machinery into a noisy green mask in frame 5, and includes the blue container inside the red-shirted worker's 'person' mask.
descriptions.pose: The body/hand skeleton map is entirely blank in frames 1 and 2 and detects only the upper body and head keypoints (yellow) of the approaching red-shirted worker on the right side of the floor in frames 3, 4, and 5 as he closes the distance from roughly 3.5 m to 1.5 m below and in front of the camera wearer. In frames 3 and 4, the torso rectangle, facial keypoints, and bent elbows show him facing forward and looking upward toward the camera wearer with both forearms angled inward around the blue containers within his arm's reach, plus two or three isolated leg keypoints below the torso where his lower legs are partly self-occluded by his upper body and the held containers from the high camera angle. By frame 5, as the camera tilts down and right, the skeleton rotates and enlarges in the lower-right quadrant, showing his shoulders and head tilted back to look directly up at the camera wearer while his arms reach upward toward the camera wearer's outstretched arm (which is about 0.5–1 m away). Compared to the shadowy RGB frames, the facial and shoulder keypoints explicitly confirm the exact frame (frame 3) when the approaching worker orients his head and chest directly toward the camera wearer and how his arm posture shifts as he lifts the container. However, the pose map is severely limited in coverage and reliability, failing to detect any skeletons for the other three workers (who are 2–6 m away and partly occluded by the cart and machinery), missing the camera wearer's own reaching arm and hand in frames 4–5, and rendering no magenta hand skeletons at all.
